name: Initialize project context
description: Analyze project and initialize knowledge structure with facts, constraints, and conventions.
whenToUse: Starting work on a new project that needs structured context for workflow agents.

team.perspective: Analyze the project structure, tech stack, and conventions to extract objective facts.
Verify extracted facts are accurate and complete, flag assumptions vs facts.
Write clear, structured context files following the knowledge structure convention.

texts.knowledge-structure:
## Knowledge Structure Convention

Files go in `.claude/context/`:
- `facts/` — Verified, objective (ALL agents read)
- `perspectives/` — Role-specific viewpoints (role-scoped)
- `decisions/` — Finalized ADRs with rationale
- `open_issues/` — Unresolved questions under debate
- `working/` — Transient task state (not authoritative)

Each file needs a header:
```yaml
---
type: fact | perspective | decision | open_issue | working
source: human | agent:<role> | consensus
confidence: verified | unverified | contested
scope: shared | role:<name>
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

**Critical rules:**
1. Only synthesizer writes to `facts/` or `decisions/` after verification
2. Other agents write to `working/` first
3. Decisions require rationale (min 20 chars)
texts.changelist-format:
## Change-list format (context-changes.json)

The artifact MUST be a single JSON object applied by `dw apply <runId>`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "changes": [
    { "op": "create", "path": "facts/architecture.md", "content": "---\ntype: fact\nsource: agent:architect\nconfidence: verified\nscope: shared\nupdated: YYYY-MM-DD\n---\n\n# Architecture\n..." }
  ]
}
```

**Rules:**
- `op`: create | update | delete
- `path`: relative to .claude/context/, starts with facts/ perspectives/ decisions/ open_issues/ working/, ends in .md
- `content`: REQUIRED for create/update (full file incl. YAML header), FORBIDDEN for delete
- The YAML header `type:` must match the folder: facts→fact, decisions→decision, open_issues→open_issue, perspectives→perspective, working→working
- `dw apply` validates paths + headers, writes atomically, and verifies with SHA-256. Any violation aborts the whole apply.

phases.title: Analyze project
phases.goal: Analyst explores project structure, reads key files (package.json, README, config files, src/ structure). Extract: tech stack, frameworks, conventions, architecture patterns, test setup, build tools.
instructions: Read package.json, tsconfig.json, and similar config files
Identify main directories and their purposes
Note coding conventions from existing code
List technologies, frameworks, and key dependencies
Output facts as structured JSON with confidence levels

phases.title: Review extracted facts
phases.goal: Reviewer verifies the extracted facts, separates verified facts from assumptions, flags anything that needs human clarification.
instructions: For each fact, verify it can be confirmed from project files
Mark as 'verified' only if you can cite the source
Mark as 'unverified' if it's an inference or assumption
Flag contradictions or unclear areas as 'contested'
List questions that need human input

phases.title: Clarify with user
phases.goal: Get user input on contested facts and project-specific conventions not evident from code.

phases.title: Build the change-list
phases.goal: Produce a deterministic change-list artifact that 'dw apply' writes to .claude/context/. Do NOT write files directly — emit the change-list only.
instructions: Emit the artifact as a SINGLE JSON object matching text:changelist-format exactly — no markdown, no prose outside the JSON
Add a create entry for facts/architecture.md with verified tech stack and patterns
Add a create entry for facts/conventions.md with coding standards
Add a create entry for facts/glossary.md if domain terms are found
Add create entries under open_issues/ for any facts too uncertain to verify
Every create carries full file content including the YAML header (type: fact or open_issue, source, confidence, scope, updated)
Do NOT write any file yourself — 'dw apply <runId>' performs the writes with path+header validation and SHA-256 verification

triggers: Project conventions are ambiguous or undocumented
Architecture decisions are not evident from code
